facts.claim: Google’s RT-1 robot model, trained on over 130,000 demonstrations collected with 13 robots over 17 months, looks and picks its next action 3 times a second.
Zhao et al.’s ALOHA arms (2023) learned each fine task, such as slotting a battery, from 50 human demonstrations, and set their joints 50 times a second.

Ross, Gordon and Bagnell (2011) showed that copying an expert breaks a basic assumption of learning, because what a robot sees next depends on what it just did; their DAgger runs the policy, has the expert label the states it reaches, and adds them.
Tobin et al. (2017) trained an object finder only on simulated images with random, unrealistic textures and lighting; on real camera images it found objects to within 1.5 cm.
